data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 proposes that evidence of a genuine reliability gain within a single evaluation is the presence of 'disagreement-resolution cycles' in panel notes. But this diagnostic fails to separate genuine reliability from checklist compliance: panel members can disagree, record a resolution, and still arrive at the right answer purely because the checklist steers them—without the disagreement reflecting deeper comprehension. Worse, the absence of disagreement cycles does not imply absence of reliability: a well-designed checklist may produce unanimous correct answers with zero disagreement, yet SRC_002's criterion would miss that gain entirely.
